sources.title: Testing the useability and applicability of Australian multilingual public service communications
sources.release_version_or_commit: 61-page public report title page says June 2023. RMIT project page separately lists project dates April 2023–June 2024; exact final report release date is not otherwise stated.
sources.locator: PDF pp. 10–14: methods, language groups, respondents and survey process; pp. 15–18: method/document preference and exceptions; pp. 19–20: respondent reasons; project page identifies commissioning body and study frame.
sources.observed_operation: Opened the RMIT University project page and 61-page linked report through the web reader; inspected methods, demographics, four-method preference tables, and stated limitations.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Commonwealth Department of Health and Aged Care commissioned a study of four COVID-19 public-health documents, translated by four methods into seven languages. It used 21 community readers (three per language) recruited across Australian states; focus groups/survey were in each respondent’s preferred language, oral or written. Four versions of each of four documents were considered in sequence with a 77-question survey. Methods 3 (Plain-English source rewrite then double human translation) and 4 (direct target-language drafting from a brief) were preferred on three documents; the fourth webpage document favored conventional translation and method 3 drew the most confusion, with font/layout/wording explanations.
sources.applicability_and_transfer_limit: The report is a useful multilingual implementation comparison because it reports audience, language, recruitment intent, tasks, language assistance, and preference/confusion outcomes. Its 3-per-language cells, sequential subjective ratings, sample skew (including Australian education and English information use), lack of objective comprehension/task-completion tests, and health-message domain limit inference. It does not choose a best method for a community-course notice or establish the center’s policy.

critic_verification.locator: Official RMIT report, pp. 3, 10-13, 15-17; RMIT project page for commission and dates.
critic_verification.observed_operation: Reopened the 61-page RMIT PDF and project page; inspected method, participant, task/outcome, demographic and result sections.
critic_verification.governing_condition_default_exception: Four Australian government COVID-19 health documents across seven languages and four methods; 21 readers (three per language) reviewed four versions in sequence and answered a survey in their preferred language. The reported A-C vs D result concerns perceived ease/preference/confusion.
critic_verification.applicability_and_transfer_limit: Useful method comparator, but small language cells, sequential subjective outcomes and health-message context do not establish a preferred method for course notices.

reviser_verification.access_time_precision: The page-level second was not captured; this bounded interval contains the direct revisit.
reviser_verification.locator: Report title page (June 2023); report pp. 10-14 for methods/sample and pp. 15-18 for document-specific preference/confusion; RMIT project page for commission and project dates. Full-PDF text search was also used to check the recruitment-route claim.
reviser_verification.observed_operation: Opened the official RMIT PDF and project page through the web reader. Inspected study frame, methods/sample, ordered exposure, survey, outcomes and results; searched report text for recruitment/recruited and likely recruitment/channel terms.
reviser_verification.governing_condition_default_exception: Four Australian government COVID-19 health documents, four translation methods, seven languages, and 21 community readers (three per language). Readers considered four versions of each document in sequence and responded to a 77-question survey in their preferred language, orally or in writing. Reported outcomes concern perceptions/preferences/confusion. Documents A-C and D show different preference patterns.
reviser_verification.applicability_and_transfer_limit: Evidence of document-specific variation in this report only. Small language cells, sequential exposure, subjective outcomes and the public-health setting do not determine a method for course enrollment or establish center policy. Methods pages state recruitment intent but do not name a recruitment channel; full-text search is not proof of global absence.

reviser_adjudications.disposition: accept scoped reading; retain original result and transfer caveat
reviser_adjudications.basis: Primary report pp. 15-18 supports Methods 3/4 preference on Documents A-C and the Document D reversal/confusion pattern; it reports perceived outcomes, not course-fee or reservation task accuracy.
reviser_adjudications.intended_claim_status: accepted: report supports the document-specific result
reviser_adjudications.diagnostic_c_star_status: rejected as unsupported: no general recommendation for multilingual notices

reviser_adjudications.diagnostic_c_star_status: rejected as unsupported: no universal all-web-systems rule

reviser_adjudications.basis: Inspected methods pages describe recruitment aims and sample but no channel; full-report text search did not locate a route, and is not treated as proof of global absence.
